title: Design System: DAK Blog — El Catálogo

provenance.derivedFrom: Shipped source: style.css, assets/css/{portada,articulo,seccion}.css, assets/js/blog.js, single.php, header.php, inc/*.php, template-parts/*.php. Values read from the built code, not from the direction contract.
provenance.productTruth: wordpress-theme/dak-informando/PRODUCT.md — still filed under the OUTGOING theme's folder. Accurate as product record; not moved or rewritten by this pass.
provenance.verifiedState: Finish review disposition: ship, nothing open. 20/20 PHP files compile. Front page, single, category and search render in real WordPress (Playground, WP 7.1 / PHP 8.3) with WP_DEBUG on and zero warnings. detect.mjs returns []. Exactly one h1 per template, no level skips.
provenance.limitation: No screenshots exist for this build, and none for the «registro de canto» entry surface either — the harness's browser pane could not composite frames. Every visual judgement was derived from source and computed values, not from seeing the render. The user confirmed the earlier live result matches the static preview; the entry surface has no such confirmation on record.
provenance.typeRampReconciliation: Second pass, 2026-08-27. detect.mjs raised 24 advisories against the 8-step ramp of the first record. A full literal inventory of the stylesheets found 13 distinct font-size literals plus 5 clamp() expressions. The record was short, not the CSS: 0.9375rem (7 uses), 0.875rem (6), 0.8125rem (5), 1rem (2) and 1.2rem (1) were genuine, pre-existing registers that the first pass skipped, and they are now named steps (secundario, control, fino, base, subtitulo). Two literals were snapped rather than blessed: .articulo-cuerpo h2 moved from 1.75rem to the documented Headline clamp and lost its mobile override, and 1.45rem was deleted as the clamp covers it. One literal remains unrecorded on purpose — see openDrift.

openDrift.action: Snap to 1.05rem (Banda). It prints the section code inside the thumbnail square, which is exactly the role Banda already names; a single-use literal 0.1rem away from an existing step is not a system step and was not canonized to make an advisory disappear.

newSurface.name: El registro de canto
newSurface.seed: surface seed 1f94094b, --scope surface --mode read, assigned candidate 6
newSurface.relationship: The entry's index is NOT a new component. It is .canto-pestana — the front page's edge tab — re-pointed from the eight catalogue sections to this entry's own h2 sections, restyled for an in-grid column instead of a viewport edge. One IntersectionObserver and one es-activa class serve both pointings; header.php suppresses the section rail on is_singular('post') so exactly one canto renders per page. A future edit must not fork these into two components.
newSurface.grounding: Sections are built from h2 (median 9, max 13 per entry across 58 published posts) so the surface works on the existing corpus without touching the _blog-content/ generator. The generated section counter was cleared against the corpus first: only 9 of 501 h2 (2%) carry their own 'N.' prefix, so the counter does not collide.

provenance.forwardNote: The _blog-content/ content contract remains deferred. The entry redesign that was previously deferred with it has now shipped as «el registro de canto» and is recorded above.
provenance.deployConstraint: The theme folder is the only versioned part of this blog. The WordPress install is administered live and has no repository; the main site deploys with rsync --delete and only spares the blog via deploy-protect.txt. Changes to this system land as theme files, never as live edits.

typeRamp.note: The closed set of size literals the theme ships, for literal-checking tools. Two rungs carry two roles each on purpose. Any value not listed here is drift.
typeRamp.floor: 0.6875rem (11px) is the floor for functional text.

casa.usage: Fill only. 4.12:1 as text on paper — structurally barred from being a letter.

casa-texto.usage: The house purple when it must be read as text on paper (6.1:1). Prose links, the folded index's disclosure marker, the share control's hover fill, and the pressed state of the purple button (white on it: 6.80:1).

casa-clara.usage: The house purple when it must be read as text on dark ink — footer links on hover, footer band titles, and the field names of the entry's data strip.

papel.usage: The page itself; also the fill of callout boxes and table headers, so a boxed note reads as paper set into the white sheet.

papel-fila.usage: The white of every row band, the header, the cover, the archive masthead, the article body and the share control at rest. Content sits on white; the page around it is grey.

papel-tinte.usage: Hover fill for rows, index cells and the entry's canto tabs; the placeholder behind an image that has not loaded.

tinta.usage: Body text, the footer's whole ground, the top identification strip, the entry's full-bleed data strip, the 3px cover rules, and the outer ring of the focus halo.

tinta-2.usage: Long-form prose colour, the minutes figure, header nav at rest, the resting canto tab and share control, bold text inside metadata.

tinta-3.usage: Secondary metadata, excerpts, column headers, placeholders, the register and canto captions, breadcrumb current item. Nothing quieter than this exists as text.

filete.usage: The hairline grid: between rows and canto tabs, around callouts, share controls and tables, under record pairs, as the register's vertical divider, and as the 1px gutter showing through index grids.

filete-fuerte.usage: The stronger hairline and the resting fill of the entry canto's number stamp: input and pagination borders, scrollbar thumb, breadcrumb separators, the rule under the back link.

sec-defecto.usage: Fallback glaze for any category outside the eight-section map. It orders last and never breaks the layout.

display.purpose: The front-page cover h1, with near-identical clamp variants on the archive masthead and the 404. Composes the LCP.

display-entrada.purpose: The article h1, tracked tighter and steeper than the cover because it sits inside the 42rem reading column rather than across the container.

headline.purpose: Two roles, one clamp: the featured entry's title on the cover and the numbered h2 section heading inside an article. The clamp is the mobile behaviour; no breakpoint override.

subtitulo.purpose: The prose h3 — the rung between a numbered section and a labelled paragraph group. h4 drops to the Banda step.

banda.purpose: The section-code step: the code and name inside a glazed band, and the prose h4. Any figure printed at band-code scale uses it.

body.purpose: Faustina article body in a 42rem column (~68 characters). Steps to 1.0625rem below 900px.

title.purpose: The catalogue row title — the reader's own question written out. The most repeated type in the system.

body-corto.purpose: Faustina at the Title size: excerpts, cover subhead, archive intro, 404 copy and callout text.

base.purpose: The document's own font-size, inherited by anything that does not opt out, and the Faustina step text of the footer's ordering procedure.

secundario.purpose: The secondary reading register: row excerpts, index entry names, the values in every data record (.edicion, .ficha-tira), the folded index, the search field, prose tables. Read after the heading, before the fine print.

control.purpose: Compact controls and stamps: footer buttons and record values, pagination numbers, the cover index code chip, the generated article-section counter. Tabular.

fino.purpose: Fine print: footer conditions and imprint, figure captions, the empty-archive notice, the entry canto's section name, the 'read entry' affordance.

dato.purpose: The price column (minutes), dates, counts and the back link. Always tabular figures.

rotulo.purpose: The catalogue small-cap at the 11px functional floor. Column headers, box captions, data-strip field names, identification strip, register and canto captions, image stamp, footer band titles. NOT for eyebrows above headings.

fonts.note: Preloaded because it composes the entire first viewport; the LCP is the h1 text.
Not preloaded: first appears in excerpts below the fold; swap is sufficient.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: This system ships zero surface shadows, zero radii and zero gradients — verified by grep across all four stylesheets. Depth is tonal layering, hairline rules and rule weight (1px → 2px → 3px). A sticky column or band stays flat and never grows a shadow to prove it is fixed.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: The only box-shadow in the theme, and it is a solid ring rather than a shadow. Two tones because a single-tone ring in --casa measured 1.70:1 against the green band and 1.77:1 against the SEO purple, below WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1. Verified across all 13 real backgrounds: paper, white row, eight glazes, dark footer, dark strip.

motion.name: avance
motion.purpose: The system's single easing token. No bounce, no second curve. Every transition in the theme uses it.

motion.name: canto-activo-borde
motion.purpose: The signature gesture in its edge pointing: the tab of the section you are reading protrudes and saturates while its neighbours stay at 0.5 opacity. Displacement is transform only, never width or margin.

motion.name: canto-activo-columna
motion.purpose: The same gesture in its column pointing, inside the entry's grid. A column has no edge to protrude from, so the identical active/resting distinction is carried by fill and ink weight instead of translation. Same class, same observer.

motion.name: filete-avanza
motion.purpose: A 2px --casa rule grows across the bottom of a hovered or focused catalogue row — a straightedge advancing under the line you are reading.

motion.name: copiado
motion.purpose: The copy-link confirmation: the control fills with the entry's own section glaze and returns. No toast, no overlay.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Honoured globally. Every canto tab remains a working link with no movement, and the folded index covers navigation if the script never runs.

breakpoints.name: canto-borde
breakpoints.purpose: Front-page edge tabs are removed; the section band becomes position: sticky instead.

breakpoints.name: canto-entrada
breakpoints.purpose: The entry's canto column is removed; a <details> folded index takes over above the body. The grid drops to register + reading column.

breakpoints.name: rejillas
breakpoints.purpose: Cover index drops to two columns; the featured box stacks and its image takes 16:9; footer index halves.

breakpoints.name: movil
breakpoints.purpose: --margen drops from 2rem to 1.25rem; header nav is replaced by a bordered link; the entry's register is removed and its share controls reappear as a ruled row at the close; the data strip becomes a two-column grid; the article-section number track narrows to 2.15rem; article type steps down; footer buttons go full-width.

breakpoints.name: fila
breakpoints.purpose: Column header is removed; the row reflows to two columns with the minutes figure on the metadata line; wide tables scroll horizontally.

breakpoints.name: cintillo
breakpoints.purpose: The optional half of the top identification strip is dropped.

breakpoints.name: ficha-tira
breakpoints.purpose: The entry's data strip goes single-column.

fila.purpose: The index unit: thumbnail, description, minutes. Shared by the column header so a list of links reads as a table. Reflows to 3.5rem | 1fr at 620px.

entrada.purpose: The reading unit: register, reading column, canto — 65.5rem inside a 78rem container, so neither margin is dead. The title header uses the same grid in column 2 so the h1 starts where the body starts. Both side columns are sticky at top: 1.5rem. Drops the canto at 1180px and the register at 900px.

apartado.purpose: The numbered article section: counter stamp in the left track, heading in the right. Narrows to 2.15rem | 1fr at 900px.

sectionMap.mechanism: dak_var_seccion($slug) in inc/helpers.php emits style="--sec:#HEX" once on the outermost element of a block. Bands, chips, both kinds of canto tab, row labels, index numbers, nav squares, the numbered-article-section stamp and the copied-link confirmation all read that same inherited variable. No component hard-codes a section hex.
sectionMap.fallback: An unmapped category gets numero '—' and --sec-defecto, and sorts last.

components.name: Tira de ficha técnica
components.description: The entry's record, flattened into a full-bleed ink strip under the title: Firma / Publicado / Revisado / Lectura / Apartados. Third appearance of the bordered data object (.edicion on the cover, .ficha-casa on the back cover). 'Revisado' only prints when the post was modified more than a day after publication; 'Apartados' is filled by script from the section count.

components.name: Apartado numerado
components.description: The article's h2, opened by a 2px --casa rule and numbered by a CSS counter into a --sec-filled stamp. The figure is generated, not authored: only 9 of 501 h2 across the 58-post corpus carry their own 'N.' prefix, so the counter appears on every published entry without touching the generator.

components.name: Registro y controles de compartir
components.description: The entry's left margin made to work: a sticky column with a vertically-set caption over square share controls, closed by a vertical hairline. Below 900px the identical control set (buffered once in PHP, printed twice) becomes a ruled horizontal row at the close. The copy button hides itself when the Clipboard API is absent, and confirms by filling with the entry's own section glaze.

narrative.overview:
This is a printed trade catalogue rendered in HTML. Not a magazine, not a documentation site, not the card grid with a photo on top and a category pill that every agency blog ships. The reader is on a phone, arrived from Google, and is deciding whether to hire DAK; the catalogue answers that by behaving like an index — sections numbered 01 through 08, each opening with a full-bleed colour band, each listing entries as rows of a table: reference, description, price. The price is minutes of reading. That single conceit governs everything below.

The material is paper and ink. Grey bond paper (#F2F2F0) carries white rows (#FFFFFF); rules are hairlines (#D4D4CE), never gaps. There are no shadows, no radii, no gradients anywhere in the shipped CSS — one box-shadow exists in the whole theme and it is the outer halo of the focus ring. Depth is entirely tonal and structural: paper behind, white row in front, black or glazed band as a hard edge. Colour is flat fill and never a tint of a tint.

The eight section glazes are the world's saturation budget, and they are spent in one place at a time: a band, a numbered chip, an edge tab. The house purple #B024FF is a separate voice from those glazes — it marks DAK itself (the edition seal, the "next step" caption, the article's section rules, the current page number) and it is a fill, never a letter.
keyCharacteristics: Grey paper with white rows; hairline rules instead of whitespace gaps.
Eight section glazes propagated through a single inherited --sec custom property.
Zero radius, zero shadow, zero gradient — the flatness is the identity, not a shortcut.
Archivo with tabular figures for all structure; Faustina for all prose.
One authored motion gesture, re-pointed rather than duplicated across surfaces.
Self-hosted variable fonts, latin subset, zero third-party origins.

rules.name: The Fill-Only Rule
rules.body: --casa is a surface, never a letter. Any purple that has to be read as text is --casa-texto on paper or --casa-clara on ink. There is no third option.

rules.name: The One Glaze Per Block Rule
rules.body: A section colour is declared exactly once, on the outermost element of its block, as --sec. Bands, chips, edge tabs, row labels, index numbers and numbered article sections all read that same variable. Never hard-code a section hex into a component.

rules.name: The Darkening Press Rule
rules.body: Interactive purple gets darker on hover, never lighter. Lightening #B024FF puts white text below 4.5:1; --casa-texto holds 6.80:1.

rules.name: The Two-Job Rule
rules.body: Archivo for structure, Faustina for prose. A heading inside article prose switches back to Archivo; an excerpt inside a structural row switches to Faustina. The face announces which job the text is doing.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number in the catalogue — codes, counts, dates, minutes, page numbers, table cells, the numbered-section counter — runs font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Columns of figures that do not align are not a catalogue.

rules.name: The Air-Above Rule
rules.body: In article prose, headings take more space above than below (h2 2.5em top, 0.7em to the next element). One rhythm, whole page.

rules.name: The Twelve-Step Rule
rules.body: The ramp is closed. A new surface picks the nearest existing step; it does not introduce a thirteenth literal. Two rungs carry two roles each on purpose (Headline serves the cover's featured title and the article's numbered section; Title and Body corto share 1.0625rem across the two faces) — that reuse is what keeps the ramp short.

rules.name: The Full-Bleed Band Rule
rules.body: Section colour reaches the edges of the viewport; the type inside it does not. Never box a section colour inside the container.

rules.name: The Hairline Gutter Rule
rules.body: Grid gaps in index surfaces are 1px of --filete showing through, not empty space. The catalogue is ruled, not spaced.

rules.name: The No-Empty-Margin Rule
rules.body: A reading column is centred by giving both margins work, not by letting them go blank. On the entry that is the register on the left and the canto on the right; when a breakpoint takes one away, its content relocates into the flow (the canto becomes a folded index above the body, the register becomes a share row at the close) rather than evaporating.

rules.name: The Flat-Ink Rule
rules.body: No shadow, no radius, no gradient, no blur. If something needs to separate from what is behind it, it gets a rule or a change of paper tone. A sticky element is not an exception.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Focus Rule
rules.body: Focus is a white 2px outline with a --tinta 5px halo outside it. A single-tone ring in the house purple measured 1.70:1 against the green section band — below the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 requires for non-text — so the ring carries both a light and a dark tone and survives all thirteen real backgrounds in the build: paper, white row, eight glazes, dark footer and dark strip.

rules.name: The No-Side-Rule Rule
rules.body: An accent rule on the left or right edge of a block is banned in this project. Callouts get a full 1px box with a 2px --casa rule across the top. The left accent bar is the most recognisable tell of a generated interface and this world does not use it. Structural column dividers — the register's vertical hairline, the data strip's field separators — are grid rules, not accents: they are --filete or 18% white, never --casa or a section glaze.

rules.name: The Third-Appearance Rule
rules.body: The bordered data object appears three times and always means the same thing — a record of the thing you are looking at, printed as label/value pairs in tabular figures. .edicion opens the front page, .ficha-tira opens the entry, .ficha-casa closes the back cover. A fourth data surface uses this object; it does not invent one.

dos: Do set the section colour once per block as --sec (via dak_var_seccion()) and let every child inherit it.
Do use --casa (#B024FF) as fill only, --casa-texto (#8B1CC7) for purple text on paper, --casa-clara (#D89BFF) for purple text on ink.
Do keep the two-tone focus ring exactly as it is: white 2px outline plus a --tinta 5px halo. It is the only ring that clears 3:1 on all thirteen real backgrounds.
Do pick a size from the twelve recorded steps. If a new surface seems to need a thirteenth, the nearest step is the answer.
Do run tabular figures on every number: codes, counts, dates, minutes, page numbers, tables, generated section numbers.
Do use Archivo for structure and Faustina for prose, switching face whenever the job changes.
Do separate with hairlines and paper-tone changes; escalate emphasis by making a rule heavier (1px → 2px → 3px), not by adding depth.
Do keep 0.6875rem (11px) as the floor for functional text.
Do keep prose at 42rem and use text-wrap: balance on every large heading.
Do give both margins of a reading column something to do, and relocate that content into the flow when the breakpoint takes the margin away.
Do re-point the canto rather than build a second index component; one canto per page, and header.php enforces it.
Do keep exactly one h1 per template with no heading-level skips.
Do self-host fonts, latin subset, and preload only the face that composes the first viewport.
Do move motion through transform and opacity, honour prefers-reduced-motion, and drive scroll state with IntersectionObserver.
Do derive structure from what the corpus already publishes (sections from h2, counts from the DOM) and verify the frequency before relying on it, as the 2%-collision check did.
Do hide a control that cannot function (the copy button with no Clipboard API) rather than ship a dead affordance.
Do give a missing image a filled section-coloured square with its number, not an empty cell.
donts: Don't add a border-radius, a box-shadow on a surface, or a gradient. The one shadow in the theme is the focus halo, and a sticky element is not an exception.
Don't put an accent rule on the left or right edge of a block. Callouts are boxed with a top rule. Structural column hairlines are --filete or a white tint, never an accent colour.
Don't write text in #B024FF on paper — it measures 4.12:1.
Don't lighten purple on hover; darken it.

Don't put a decorative label above a heading. No eyebrows, no kickers anywhere. The Rótulo style is for box captions, column headers, data-strip field names and the image stamp; the section chip may precede an h1 only because it is a working link to that section's archive.
Don't ship the card grid with a photo on top and a category pill. Entries are rows in a table.
Don't let a row thumbnail compete with the featured box: thumbnails are thumbnail-size, lazy and desaturated at rest; exactly one image per page loads eagerly.
Don't hide breadcrumbs or any element that carries structured data.
Don't hard-code a section hex into a component; read --sec.
Don't add a per-heading size override at a breakpoint when the heading is already set with a clamp() — the clamp is the mobile behaviour.

Don't register add_image_size(). WordPress's proportional defaults already exist on the server for all live posts and give a real srcset immediately; a custom crop would force a full thumbnail regeneration on a live install that has no repository.

Don't reintroduce a per-entry catalogue code. The 01–08 section numbering and the generated article-section counter are the ordering devices; a database ID printed on a row was noise and was removed at the user's request.
Don't animate width or margin, and don't add a second authored motion gesture — the canto is the site's one flourish, in both of its pointings.
